speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition better, can you describe the appearance of the rash on your trunk and extremities? Is it raised, flat, or does it look like small red spots?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see, so the facial rash appeared a week after the initial fever and spared the perioral area? This sounds like a classic "slapped cheek" appearance. Do you recall if she was recently exposed to anyone with a similar rash or respiratory infection?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of a "slapped cheek" facial rash that spares the perioral area, followed by a lacy, pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities, along with mild prodromal symptoms, is classic for Fifth Disease. DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
